answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. This is resilient because unearned rewards are capped and eventually burned, so an attacker cannot bank on a runaway Sybil campaign paying off. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a harbor as the anchor of the cost.
